avalanche.travel_advice: Watch for signs of unstable snow such as recent avalanches, cracking in the snow, and audible collapsing. Avoid traveling on or under similar slopes.

facts: No new snow measured at the 3 nearby stations in the 72 hours to Sep 29.

facts.text: Snow left Lyman Lake (5,990 ft) 1 day later this year than the median of the three earlier seasons on file (2023 to 2025).

evidence.name: Lyman Lake
evidence.detail: left June 13; earlier seasons: June 11 (2023), June 25 (2024), June 12 (2025)

facts.text: At Lyman Lake (5,990 ft), this year's highest snow water on or after April 1 was 48.8 in, the second highest of the four seasons on file (2023 to 2026).

evidence.name: Lyman Lake
evidence.detail: 48.8 in on April 4; earlier seasons: 52.8 in (2023), 37.7 in (2024), 42.8 in (2025)

facts.text: An estimate: snow left the pass itself between May 9 and July 9, carried from the melt-out dates at 3 nearby stations to the pass elevation.

evidence.name: Decline Creek
evidence.detail: melted out May 18, 1,228 ft below the pass; points to May 9 to July 9

evidence.name: Deer Pass
evidence.detail: melted out April 23, 2,348 ft below the pass; points to April 25 to July 12

evidence.name: Lyman Lake
